title: Context-aware thresholding and outage telemetry orchestration
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Build a context-aware orchestration layer that converts low-level tracing and metric signals into prioritized, composite SLO alerts and outage telemetry. This ticket implements the core pieces: 1) lightweight tracing hooks to attach request-context tags (customer_tier, route_version, cost_class) to spans emitted in the runtime; 2) enrichment stage in the metrics/logs pipeline (Kafka -> enrichment worker -> metricstore) that correlates traces with latency histograms and error counters; 3) an alert scoring engine that computes composite severity across multiple SLOs and decides paging windows based on ongoing outage characteristics. Rationale: existing burn-rate alerts are noisy during multi-customer correlated spikes and don't account for contextual mitigations (canary rollbacks, autoscaler events). By adding contextual metadata and a scoring layer we can reduce false positives and route pages to the right oncall team with a recommended remediation action. Scope: phased rollout (A: instrumentation + pipeline enrichment; B: scoring engine + policy rules; C: canary and global rollout).
comments: 2026-02-18 - Sofia Martinez: Created ticket after postmortem for 2026-02-15 latency blip. Noted correlation between autoscaler events and multiple customer burn-rate fires. Proposed context-enrichment approach in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Context-aware+Alerting

2026-02-22 - Rohit Patel: Spike complete. Implemented prototype tracing hook that tags spans with 'rw.customer_tier' and 'rw.route_version'. Observed 0.4% p99 span size increase. Trade-off: richer context increases trace volume and storage; plan to use sampling + prefix cache to limit retention.

2026-02-28 - Lila Huang (SRE): Reviewed enrichment plan. Concern: enrichment worker can add 300-400ms worst-case latency for synchronous pipelines. Decision: do enrichment asynchronously into metricstore and attach a small 'enrichment_pending' flag to alerts for immediate triage. Follow-up: add deduplicator in scoring engine.

2026-03-03 - Rohit Patel: Opened PR for tracing hook and SDK changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4892. Added new span attribute mapping and unit tests. Needs design + security review for PII tags exclusion.

2026-03-07 - Security (Aditi Rao): Approved tagging whitelist; added requirement to redact any user-identifiers and confirm KMS rotation before retention increase. See security note: https://drive.redwood.ai/secure/obs-tagging-constraints.pdf

2026-03-10 - Data Eng (Marco): Enrichment worker MVP deployed to staging. Verified correlation join latency 90th=120ms, 99th=420ms. Will add an async backpressure queue and backfill job for historical joins. Linked dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/alerts/context-enrichment

2026-03-12 - Rohit Patel: Implemented scoring engine prototype in Go. Scoring rules configured as YAML; supports weight per SLO and dynamic windowing. Tests: lower false positive rate by ~32% on synthetic replay. Next: wire routing policies and paging windows, prepare canary run for two internal tenants (dev and partner-1).
acceptance_criteria: Tracing hooks present in runtime and enabled behind feature flag; spans include rw.customer_tier and rw.route_version without PII
Enrichment worker running in staging and producing correlated metrics joined to traces for 99% of sampled traces
Scoring engine computes composite severity and outputs a recommended paging window (immediate / 30m wait / suppress)
Canary with two internal tenants shows at least 20% reduction in pages for non-service-impacting burn-rate events
Runbooks updated with new triage fields and example incidents: Confluence runbook link included

Expose scoring policy editor in Console (PM + Design to scope)
